arjuni.hint: the two Phalgunīs — Zosma/Chertan group and Denebola

arundhati.hint: Alcor, the faint companion of Mizar in the Big Dipper's handle

bahu.hint: 'the two Arms' of the deer/Orion: usually taken as Betelgeuse and Bellatrix

invaka.hint: alternative Taittirīya name of Mṛgaśīrṣa - the stars of Orion's head

ishus-trikanda.hint: Orion's Belt - Mintaka, Alnilam, Alnitak - as the 'three-jointed arrow'

kattika-karttika.hint: Alcyone (Pleiades) — the star that names the month

krittika-seven.hint: the seven individual stars of the Pleiades

mulabarhana.members_note: 'the Scorpion's tail as a whole' — the note draws no boundary, and the tail's extent is not stated by any source here.

rksha.hint: Ursa Major (the Seven Ṛṣis / Big Dipper)

sakvara.hint: the circumpolar 14-star figure (a second name for the Śiśumāra)

saptarshi.hint: the Big Dipper - seven bright stars of Ursa Major (Dubhe, Merak, Phecda, Megrez, Alioth, Mizar, Alkaid)

shishumara.hint: the celestial porpoise/dolphin — a whole star-figure, not a single star

tishya.hint: the later Puṣya: the Asellus stars and Praesepe region

trishanku.hint: Triśaṅku — a king fixed head-downward in the southern sky

gajavithi.note: Matsya 124.55 as transmitted repeats the name नागवीथी here; Gajavīthī is the required reading.

govithi.note: Drawn on the Matsya reading. Bṛhat Saṃhitā 9.2cd gives Govīthī = Aśvinī, Revatī and the two Bhādrapadās — close to the Matsya, adding only Aśvinī. The Hasta/Citrā/Svāti version belongs to the sequential scheme at BS 9.1, which Varāhamihira attributes to others.

jaradgava.note: Drawn on the Matsya reading (vāruṇa = Śatabhiṣaj), which Bṛhat Saṃhitā 9.3ab confirms exactly: the triad beginning at Śravaṇa.

ajavithi.note: Drawn on the Matsya 124.53 / Viṣṇu 2.8.85 reading (Mūla + both Aṣāḍhās). Matsya 124.58, in the same chapter, instead gives Hasta, Citrā and Svātī — the text contradicts itself.

vaishvanari.note: Matsya 124.59 gives Vaiśvānarī the same three asterisms that 124.53 gives Ajavīthī, so the two roads are drawn on top of each other here. The contradiction is the text's, not the chart's.

local:milky-way.members_note: The galactic band; drawn as a band, not as member stars.

local:nak-vishakha.hint: Viśākhā ι Librae (with α, β Librae)

local:orions-belt.hint: Orion's Belt δ, ε, ζ Orionis

local:pisces.hint: suggested by the recorders as Pisces —

local:regulus.hint: Regulus and the stars of Maghā α, γ, ζ, η, ν Leonis

local:scorpius.hint: Shaula and the Scorpion's sting λ Scorpii and the ε–υ chain

local:taurus.hint: unidentified — a star of Taurus, apparent magnitude 3.40 as printed the Greek letter is unreadable in the source

local:ursa-minor.hint: circumpolar figure — glossed 'the Big Bear' but described as a lizard-shaped chain ending at Polaris
